newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end down on surging bond yields.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end down on surging bond yields.

text.p: Swedish shares ended lower on Tuesday, depressed by surging bond yields.

"If bond yields keep climbing you might get a good investment alternative...previously there has been no alternative to the bourse," a trader said, forecasting that share prices could keep falling if bonds continue to rise.
The exchange's general index dropped 1.89 percent to 2,684.05 in turnover of 7.52 billion crowns.
Heavyweights telecoms group Ericsson and drugs major Astra both drop with Ericsson falling eight crowns to 261 and Astra shedding five to land at 355.
"U.S. technology shares are doing poorly," a trader said, explaining Ericsson's fall.
Banking group S-E-Banken rose 2.5 crowns to 84.5 after news that its chief executive Bjorn Svedberg will resign and be replaced by Jacob Wallenberg.

Analysts said the resignation could be related to the Wallenberg family, which holds 18 percent in the bank, wanting to see a merger. Merger talks with Nordbanken failed in February. Svedberg denied this view.
Automotive group Volvo fell 3.5 to 185 after news its chairman Bert-Olof Svanholm had died.
Media group Kinnevik continued to fall, plummeting 16 crowns to 204, after presenting a lower than expected profit for 1996 on Monday.
JP Bank rose one crown to 42.5 crowns in the hope of a bid in the wake of Den Danske Bank's bid for Ostgota Enskilda Banken on Monday.
